Perfect! I've fixed the issue. The problem was that in the `calculateRoute` function, there was a local variable `device` that was shadowing the class property `device`. The local variable was of type `CLLocationCoordinate2D` (from `deviceCoordinate`), but the code was trying to access `.DeviceID` on it, which doesn't exist for that type.

The fix was to change `device.DeviceID` to `self.device.DeviceID` to explicitly reference the class property instead of the local variable. This way, we're accessing the `DeviceID` property from the `KnownDevice` object rather than trying to access it from a `CLLocationCoordinate2D`.

The error should now be resolved. The code will correctly use the device ID from the class property for caching the route information.
